items.title: Traffic accident on Multan’s Bosan Road kills 5 men in their 20s
items.description:
A road accident on Multan’s Bosan Road claimed the lives of five men in their 20s early on Monday after their speeding Toyota Corolla hit a road divider before crashing into the wall of a nearby plot and catching fire, Rescue 1122 said.
All five occupants, who were residents of Shujaabad, died at the scene.
“As a result of the accident, five individuals traveling in the car sustained severe injuries and died on the spot,” Rescue 1122 said.

items.title: Oil-rich Alberta vote to determine next step towards possible separation from Canada
items.description:
Alberta decides Monday if it wants to pursue a binding referendum on leaving Canada, with Prime Minister Mark Carney warning a separatist win would bring dangerous uncertainty during a trade war with the United States.
Polls indicate less than a quarter of people in the western Canadian province support independence.
But attention has focused on turnout in the days before the vote, and whether a motivated separatist camp could defy the polls, helped by complacent federalists.

items.description:
EVEN 128 years after his death, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan lives on. Born on Oct 17, 1817, Sir Syed passed away in 1898, but he has been endowed with Hayaat-i-Javed, or the eternal life, it seems. items.title: Agriculture: The growing threat of double-rice cropping
items.description:
Rice is Pakistan’s second-largest crop after wheat and the country’s largest agricultural export commodity. For decades, the Punjab government consistently enforced a ban on raising rice nurseries before May 20 under the Punjab Agricultural Pests Ordinance, 1959, and its 1960 Rules. Its violation was treated as a cognizable offence.

items.title: Learnings from winners of Nobel Prize in Economics
items.description:
Many Pakistani economists had tipped Susan Athey, celebrated for her groundbreaking work on internet search auctions and digital marketplaces, for this year’s Nobel Prize in Economics. However, the winners, American economists, Michael Woodford and Robert Hall, also command a devoted following among their Pakistani peers.

items.title: Bhabara Bazaar offers a glimpse into Rawalpindi’s forgotten past
items.description:
The Path Shala (school) building stands tall in Bhabara Bazaar. The building reflects the architectural taste of Bhabara’s traders.
    
Once an upscale locality of Rawalpindi under British rule, Bhabara Bazaar recalls the region’s majestic past in the heart of the garrison city.
Centuries may have passed, but the area still has many structures that reflect the splendour of Mughal, Central Asian and Indian architecture.
